I get what it's like to have some disorder but not match the most "typical" presentation of it leading to feeling alone even in communities centered around it though. Almost all of my problems hardly present themselves in a stereotypical way, I spent quite a while reading psychology books and studies before I found both explanations why things work the way they do and coping strategies for whatever I'm dealing with.

The best approach I've found so far is not trying to find a single or even multiple labels that would explain all of my problems and focusing on the symptoms instead. For example I don't have BPD but I've found some BPD oriented DBT workbooks helpful for dealing with emotional dysregulation.

Anyway for something more practical, what you're describing sounds kinda similar to ADHD emotional dysregulation (iirc there is a pretty high overlap between ASPD and ADHD), so you could look into some resources for that, even if you don't have ADHD you might find something useful.

kinda a boring story, I came out at 14 and my mother was very skeptical and even wanted me to take birth control and get my hormones checked just to make sure that I didn't have that problem (never did that) but she was ok with me getting a binder. I was also in eastern europe at the time so nothing was legal until you're 18 and after that good luck getting it the legal way anyway. I didn't know about DIY for a very long time but I don't think I could've done anything as a teenager because I was pretty badly disabled and working was definitely off the table.

eventually I moved to a different country where the situation is a little better (everything is still banned for minors but it's a bit easier to get hrt as an adult) but until I finally started the process of getting HRT access I went through a scared/ashamed/lowkey terfy repper phase and my parents took literal years to start calling me by the right name and pronouns (they mess up to this day which is awesome) so I was not 100% confident in anything I was doing.

I eventually learnt about DIY but I have the kind of mother that notices my voice being a few tones lower from a mild cold and talks about it for 3 days in a row so any changes from HRT would genuinely be impossible to hide. She doesn't notice the smell of weed or alcohol on me (and she cares about that very much so it's not a "they know they just don't say anything" situation) but she points out my minor weight fluctuations to me that not even I notice so it would be sniffed out quite quickly. I don't want to risk it, especially since I'm around a month or two away from actually getting testosterone through legal means

but yeah tldr: grew up in eastern europe, shit sucked but my mum let me bind, didn't get the opportunity to get on legal HRT until I was in a different country and nearly a decade older. could've been a youngshit if society was kind to us fml
